title: Implement routing policy: map Dedicated tier → hardware pool/shape selection
creator: Ethan Park
description:
We need a deterministic and auditable mapping from customer Dedicated tier (Standard/Plus/Premium) to eligible hardware pools/shapes in the router/orchestration layer.

This is required to:
- enforce tier-specific throughput floors by ensuring requests land on the right capacity class
- preserve Dedicated isolation semantics while still allowing defined burst/failover behaviors
- make capacity accounting and Sales quoting consistent (tier → shape families per region)

Scope:
1) Add tier-aware pool selection in routing policy for Dedicated deployments.
2) Wire to control-plane config so policy can be changed without redeploying the router.
3) Implement safe defaults + feature-flag rollout.
4) Emit routing decision telemetry (selected_pool, reason, fallbacks) to support SLO debugging.

Non-goals:
- Designing the final shape catalog (owned by Infra)
- Implementing admission control/overload shedding (ENG-19257)
- Pricing/billing logic beyond emitting tier + pool identifiers (ENG-19302)

Primary stakeholders: Product Dedicated (Lauren Bishop), Infra/Fleet (Irene Choi / Vanessa Ortiz), SRE (Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes), Observability (Allison Grant / Sergio Costa).
problem_statement: Today the router selects Dedicated capacity largely via static per-deployment configuration and/or best-effort pool matching. With tiers, we must ensure (a) the committed tier is enforced, (b) the customer cannot be silently routed to an underpowered/unsupported pool, and (c) when a tier includes burst/failover, the policy is explicit and observable. Without this, we cannot credibly measure or defend a throughput SLO and we will create support ambiguity during incidents.
proposed_approach:
Add a tier-aware pool selector that computes an ordered candidate list of pools for each request based on:
- deployment_id (Dedicated)
- tier: Standard | Plus | Premium
- region (requested + allowed failover regions)
- model_id + model_family
- max_context / requested_max_tokens (shape constraints)
- explicit overrides (deployment-pinned shape/pool)

Selection rules (high-level):
- Standard: route only to Standard-eligible pools in the requested region. No cross-region failover by default. If no pool available, return capacity error (do not degrade to lower tier pool).
- Plus: route to Plus-eligible pools in region; if Plus pool saturated/unavailable, may route to defined burst pool (same region) if enabled for deployment; if burst disabled or exhausted, return capacity error.
- Premium: route to Premium primary pool; if primary unhealthy/unavailable, route to Premium warm-spare pool in-region; optional cross-region failover (explicitly enabled) to Premium pool in secondary region.

Precedence:
1) Explicit per-deployment pin (pool_id/shape_id) wins. Tier policy is validated against pin at provisioning time (Infra runbook), and router enforces a hard check that pin remains tier-compatible.
2) Otherwise, tier policy selects eligible pools.

Implementation detail:
- Introduce control-plane config object: routing_policy.dedicated.tier_pool_map (versioned)
- Router fetches + caches policy (with TTL + fast invalidation hook)
- Router attaches tags to request context: dedicated_tier, selected_pool_id, selection_reason, fallback_hops
- Expose debug header for internal use (x-redwood-routing-decision) behind admin auth
acceptance_criteria:
- For a Dedicated deployment with tier set, router selects only pools eligible for that tier in the specified region.
- Misconfiguration (tier incompatible with pinned pool/shape, or unsupported model for tier) yields an explicit error in logs/metrics and a deterministic client error (no silent reroute).
- Plus/Premium burst/failover behaviors are gated by explicit deployment flags and are observable in metrics.
- Routing decision metrics are emitted with labels: deployment_id, tier, model_id, region, selected_pool_id, selection_reason.
- Feature flag allows per-deployment enablement and instant rollback to previous selector.
- Unit tests cover: tier compatibility, precedence rules, empty candidate lists, burst enabled/disabled, cross-region failover toggle, and model context constraints.
- Load test / replay shows no p95 routing latency regression > 2ms in router service.
implementation_notes:
Key files/components:
- router/orchestrator: DedicatedPoolSelector (new)
- control-plane client: fetch dedicated tier policy + deployment flags
- config schema: DedicatedRoutingPolicy v1 (versioned)
- telemetry: counter + histogram for selection + rejections; structured log for hard failures

Guardrails:
- Hard deny if model is not in pool.supported_models OR requested context > pool.max_context.
- Do not attempt more than N=2 fallbacks per request (avoid long tail latency).
- Ensure selection is stable for a given (deployment_id, model_id, region) when multiple pools are equivalent (consistent hashing on request_id) to reduce cache fragmentation.

Notes from SRE:
- Selection_reason must distinguish: primary, burst, warm_spare, cross_region_failover, config_override.
- Emit a separate metric for "eligible_pool_empty" to help isolate capacity vs misconfig.

Notes from Infra:
- Pool eligibility is derived from pool labels (tier_eligible=[...], shape_family, supported_models, max_context). Router should not encode hard GPU assumptions.
testing_plan:
1) Unit tests for selector ordering + denial conditions.
2) Integration test in staging with three synthetic pools (standard/plus/premium) and a fake model constraint.
3) Shadow mode: emit "would_select_pool_id" alongside existing selector for 48 hours on 3 internal Dedicated deployments.
4) Canary enablement for 2 beta customers selected in PM rollout (one Plus, one Premium) with Observability dashboard watch.
5) Failure injection: mark primary pool unhealthy and validate Premium warm spare selection; simulate burst pool saturation and validate Plus fallback behavior + error return.
rollout_plan:
Feature flag: dedicated_tier_pool_selector
- Phase 0 (staging): enabled for all Dedicated staging deployments.
- Phase 1 (shadow): production, flag off; emit comparison logs/metrics only.
- Phase 2 (canary): enable per-deployment for beta accounts (per PM beta list); monitor routing errors, SLO burn signals, and customer tickets.
- Phase 3 (expand): enable for all new Dedicated deployments; then migrate existing deployments tier-by-tier.

Rollback:
- Flip flag off per deployment (instant).
- Control-plane policy can be reverted to previous version if needed.

Owner on rollout day: Mina Haddad; oncall coordination with Rafael Mendes (SRE) and Vanessa Ortiz (Fleet).
deliverables: Control-plane routing policy schema + cached fetch path
open_questions: Do we allow Standard cross-region failover in any scenario? (Decision: no; require explicit Premium failover flag only.)
What is the contract if a customer pins a pool that later becomes tier-ineligible? (Decision: router hard-denies; provisioning must prevent this and Support escalates.)
How to handle multi-model Dedicated deployments with different context needs? (Decision: router selects per-model; provisioning should create model-specific pools if required.)
status_updates: 2025-02-03 (Mina): Drafted selector interface + control-plane policy shape; aligning labels with Infra pool metadata.
2025-02-10 (Elena): Implemented candidate ordering + stable hashing; added initial metrics but missing selection_reason cardinality review.
2025-02-14 (Rafael): Requested explicit "eligible_pool_empty" signal + hard cap on fallback attempts to protect tail latency.
2025-02-20 (Mina): Added feature flag + shadow mode comparator; integrated with deployment flags for burst/failover toggles.
2025-02-27 (Sergio): Added dashboard panels consuming selected_pool_id/selection_reason; confirmed tags are usable without exploding cardinality.
2025-03-06 (Mina): PR approved + merged; started staging soak; scheduled production shadow enablement with oncall.
comments: Lauren Bishop (2025-02-05): We need to be able to explain in plain terms what happens when Plus is saturated. Please make sure selection_reason maps cleanly to tier entitlements (primary vs burst) so CS can answer questions without reading code.

Irene Choi (2025-02-07): Please do not hardcode GPU types in router; pool labels must be the contract. Also enforce max_context based on pool metadata; we’ve seen customers accidentally request 32k on shapes sized for 8k and it destroys throughput.
Allison Grant (2025-02-12): Add a structured log event for all hard-deny cases with a single error_code field. We’ll use it to drive an alert panel and reduce time-to-triage for SLO misses.

Sean Gallagher (2025-02-18): For SLO measurement we need a stable attribution: deployment_id and tier must be present on every request that hits Dedicated. Please ensure tags are added before any retries/fallbacks so we don’t lose the lineage in metrics.
Vanessa Ortiz (2025-03-03): Canary customers should avoid regions with constrained supply this month. Recommend starting with us-east Plus and eu-west Premium where we have warm spares.
closure_notes:
Merged via redwood/pr-19366-routing-tier-to-pool-selector. Shadow mode ran ~72h with no meaningful divergence for pinned deployments; uncovered one mis-labeled pool (tier_eligible missing Plus) which was fixed by Fleet.

Follow-ups created:
- Ensure provisioning validation fails fast when tier→pool incompatibility is detected (Infra runbook update)
- Add runbook section for interpreting selection_reason during SLO incidents (SRE/CS enablement)

Operational note: Selection_reason label set is intentionally small to keep metrics cardinality bounded.
